items.stem: The Harlem Renaissance produced an extraordinary flowering of African American literature, art, and music in the 1920s. Yet most Harlem Renaissance artists lived in poverty, owned none of the publishing houses or record companies that distributed their work, and catered to white audiences at clubs like the Cotton Club where Black patrons were not permitted. What tension does this situation reveal about the Harlem Renaissance?
items.stemEs: El Renacimiento de Harlem produjo un extraordinario florecimiento de la literatura, el arte y la música afroamericanos en la década de 1920. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los artistas del Renacimiento de Harlem vivían en la pobreza, no eran dueños de las casas editoriales ni de las compañías discográficas que distribuían su trabajo, y actuaban para audiencias blancas en clubes como el Cotton Club donde no se permitían clientes negros. ¿Qué tensión revela esta situación sobre el Renacimiento de Harlem?

choices.text: Harlem Renaissance artists achieved both cultural recognition and equal economic participation in American society.
choices.textEs: Los artistas del Renacimiento de Harlem lograron tanto el reconocimiento cultural como la participación económica igualitaria en la sociedad estadounidense.

choices.text: The Harlem Renaissance failed to achieve cultural recognition, and its artists remained largely unknown outside of African American communities.
choices.textEs: El Renacimiento de Harlem no logró el reconocimiento cultural, y sus artistas permanecieron en gran medida desconocidos fuera de las comunidades afroamericanas.

choices.text: African Americans achieved extraordinary cultural production while remaining economically marginalized, as white-controlled institutions captured the financial benefits of Black artistic genius.
choices.textEs: Los afroamericanos lograron una producción cultural extraordinaria mientras permanecían marginados económicamente, ya que las instituciones controladas por blancos capturaban los beneficios financieros del genio artístico negro.

choices.text: Harlem Renaissance artists deliberately chose to perform for white audiences because they had no interest in addressing the concerns of their own communities.
choices.textEs: Los artistas del Renacimiento de Harlem eligieron deliberadamente actuar para audiencias blancas porque no tenían interés en abordar las preocupaciones de sus propias comunidades.

items.explanation: The Harlem Renaissance created a paradox: African Americans produced celebrated art that asserted their humanity and cultural genius, yet the economic infrastructure (publishing, recording, venues) remained controlled by white intermediaries who profited from and sometimes limited access to that art. This cultural achievement coexisted with structural economic subordination. C captures this contradiction. A ignores the economic exploitation dimension entirely. B misrepresents the Renaissance as a failure; it was artistically celebrated. D is a reductive claim about artistic motivation that misrepresents the movement's actual purpose.
items.explanationEs: El Renacimiento de Harlem creó una paradoja: los afroamericanos produjeron arte celebrado que afirmaba su humanidad y genio cultural, pero la infraestructura económica (editorial, discográfica, locales) permanecía controlada por intermediarios blancos que se beneficiaban de ese arte y a veces limitaban el acceso a él. Este logro cultural coexistía con la subordinación económica estructural. C captura esta contradicción. A ignora por completo la dimensión de explotación económica. B malinterpreta el Renacimiento como un fracaso; fue artísticamente celebrado. D es una afirmación reductiva sobre la motivación artística que malinterpreta el propósito real del movimiento.

items.stem: Langston Hughes's 1926 essay "The Negro Artist and the Racial Mountain" argued that Black artists who tried to imitate white artistic standards or appeal primarily to white audiences were abandoning their most powerful creative resource — their authentic African American experience and cultural heritage. What does Hughes's argument reveal about the relationship between artistic identity and racial politics in the 1920s?
items.stemEs: El ensayo de Langston Hughes de 1926 'El artista negro y la montaña racial' argumentaba que los artistas negros que intentaban imitar los estándares artísticos blancos o apelar principalmente a audiencias blancas estaban abandonando su recurso creativo más poderoso: su experiencia afroamericana auténtica y su herencia cultural. ¿Qué revela el argumento de Hughes sobre la relación entre la identidad artística y la política racial en la década de 1920?

choices.text: Authentic African American artistic expression was itself a political act, challenging white supremacist assumptions by celebrating Black cultural identity without apology.
choices.textEs: La expresión artística afroamericana auténtica era en sí misma un acto político, desafiando las suposiciones supremacistas blancas al celebrar la identidad cultural negra sin disculpas.

choices.text: Hughes believed that Black artists should create separate institutions entirely isolated from white cultural influence to develop an authentically African art form.
choices.textEs: Hughes creía que los artistas negros debían crear instituciones separadas completamente aisladas de la influencia cultural blanca para desarrollar una forma de arte auténticamente africana.

choices.text: Hughes's essay was primarily a commercial argument, advising Black artists to market their work to African American consumers rather than white patrons.
choices.textEs: El ensayo de Hughes fue principalmente un argumento comercial, aconsejando a los artistas negros que comercializaran su trabajo para consumidores afroamericanos en lugar de patrocinadores blancos.

choices.text: Hughes argued that Black artists could achieve the greatest influence by mastering European artistic traditions and using them to assimilate into mainstream American culture.
choices.textEs: Hughes argumentaba que los artistas negros podían lograr la mayor influencia al dominar las tradiciones artísticas europeas y usarlas para asimilarse a la cultura estadounidense convencional.

items.explanation: Hughes argued that authentic Black artistic expression was itself a political act — that celebrating African American culture without apology challenged white supremacist assumptions about Black inferiority and asserted the full humanity of Black people. A captures this politicized artistic vision. B misrepresents Hughes as advocating for separatism; he argued for authentic expression, not isolation. C is a reductive commercial reading that misses Hughes's political intent. D inverts Hughes's argument; he was critiquing assimilation, not advocating for it.
items.explanationEs: Hughes argumentaba que la expresión artística negra auténtica era en sí misma un acto político: que celebrar la cultura afroamericana sin disculpas desafiaba las suposiciones supremacistas blancas sobre la inferioridad negra y afirmaba la plena humanidad de los negros. A captura esta visión artística politizada. B malinterpreta a Hughes como abogando por el separatismo; argumentaba a favor de la expresión auténtica, no del aislamiento. C es una lectura comercial reductiva que pasa por alto la intención política de Hughes. D invierte el argumento de Hughes; estaba criticando la asimilación, no abogando por ella.

items.stem: Louis Armstrong's innovations in jazz improvisation fundamentally changed American music. He shifted jazz from an ensemble-centered collective improvisation form to one centered on individual virtuoso soloing. Zora Neale Hurston, writing from an anthropologist's perspective, argued that African American folk culture carried its own sophisticated intellectual and artistic traditions. What common theme connects Armstrong's musical contribution to Hurston's cultural argument?
items.stemEs: Las innovaciones de Louis Armstrong en la improvisación del jazz cambiaron fundamentalmente la música estadounidense. Desplazó el jazz de una forma de improvisación colectiva centrada en el conjunto a una centrada en el solo virtuoso individual. Zora Neale Hurston, escribiendo desde una perspectiva de antropóloga, argumentaba que la cultura folclórica afroamericana llevaba sus propias tradiciones intelectuales y artísticas sofisticadas. ¿Qué tema común conecta la contribución musical de Armstrong con el argumento cultural de Hurston?

choices.text: Both Armstrong and Hurston argued that individual African American artists, rather than communities, were the primary sources of cultural innovation.
choices.textEs: Tanto Armstrong como Hurston argumentaban que los artistas afroamericanos individuales, en lugar de las comunidades, eran las principales fuentes de innovación cultural.

choices.text: Both figures believed that African American integration into white cultural institutions was the most effective path toward racial equality.
choices.textEs: Ambas figuras creían que la integración afroamericana en las instituciones culturales blancas era el camino más efectivo hacia la igualdad racial.

choices.text: Both Armstrong and Hurston were primarily interested in preserving African American culture as a historical artifact rather than as a living creative tradition.
choices.textEs: Tanto Armstrong como Hurston estaban principalmente interesados en preservar la cultura afroamericana como un artefacto histórico en lugar de como una tradición creativa viva.

choices.text: Both demonstrated that African American creative and intellectual traditions possessed inherent value and originality that required no validation from European cultural standards.
choices.textEs: Ambos demostraron que las tradiciones creativas e intelectuales afroamericanas poseían un valor y una originalidad inherentes que no requerían validación de los estándares culturales europeos.

items.explanation: Both Armstrong and Hurston asserted — through music and scholarship respectively — that African American creative and intellectual traditions had inherent value, sophistication, and originality that required no validation from European standards. D correctly identifies this common assertion of cultural self-worth. A conflates different aspects of their work; Armstrong emphasized individual expression and Hurston documented community culture. B misrepresents both figures' orientations toward integration. C is an incomplete reading that focuses on method rather than the substantive cultural argument both were making.
items.explanationEs: Tanto Armstrong como Hurston afirmaron, a través de la música y la beca respectivamente, que las tradiciones creativas e intelectuales afroamericanas tenían un valor, sofisticación y originalidad inherentes que no requerían validación de los estándares europeos. D identifica correctamente esta afirmación común de autoestima cultural. A conflate diferentes aspectos de su trabajo; Armstrong enfatizaba la expresión individual y Hurston documentaba la cultura comunitaria. B malinterpreta la orientación de ambas figuras hacia la integración. C es una lectura incompleta que se centra en el método en lugar del argumento cultural sustantivo que ambos hacían.

items.stem: In the 1920s, both Harlem Renaissance intellectuals and Garveyite nationalists sought to build African American identity and community — but through fundamentally different strategies. Renaissance figures like W.E.B. Du Bois sought to demonstrate Black cultural equality through artistic achievement and integration into American civic life, while Garvey sought separate Black nationhood. What does the coexistence of these competing visions reveal about the nature of Black political thought in the 1920s?
items.stemEs: En la década de 1920, tanto los intelectuales del Renacimiento de Harlem como los nacionalistas garveyistas buscaban construir identidad y comunidad afroamericanas, pero a través de estrategias fundamentalmente diferentes. Figuras del Renacimiento como W.E.B. Du Bois buscaban demostrar la igualdad cultural negra a través del logro artístico y la integración en la vida cívica estadounidense, mientras que Garvey buscaba una nacionalidad negra separada. ¿Qué revela la coexistencia de estas visiones en competencia sobre la naturaleza del pensamiento político negro en la década de 1920?

choices.text: African Americans held genuinely diverse political visions, with different communities making different rational assessments of which liberation strategies were viable given the realities of American racism.
choices.textEs: Los afroamericanos tenían visiones políticas genuinamente diversas, con diferentes comunidades haciendo diferentes evaluaciones racionales sobre qué estrategias de liberación eran viables dadas las realidades del racismo estadounidense.

choices.text: The competition between Renaissance integrationism and Garveyite nationalism demonstrates that one strategy was entirely correct and the other was entirely mistaken about how to achieve racial equality.
choices.textEs: La competencia entre el integracionismo del Renacimiento y el nacionalismo garveyista demuestra que una estrategia era completamente correcta y la otra estaba completamente equivocada sobre cómo lograr la igualdad racial.

choices.text: Both the Harlem Renaissance and Garveyism rejected mainstream American society equally and advocated for the same goal of complete Black separation from white institutions.
choices.textEs: Tanto el Renacimiento de Harlem como el Garveyismo rechazaron igualmente la sociedad estadounidense convencional y abogaron por el mismo objetivo de completa separación negra de las instituciones blancas.

choices.text: Most African Americans in the 1920s agreed with Garvey's nationalist approach, and Renaissance integrationism represented only a small elite minority within the Black community.
choices.textEs: La mayoría de los afroamericanos en la década de 1920 estaban de acuerdo con el enfoque nacionalista de Garvey, y el integracionismo del Renacimiento representaba solo una pequeña minoría élite dentro de la comunidad negra.

items.explanation: The coexistence of integrationist and nationalist strategies within Black political thought reflects that African Americans were not a monolithic political community but a diverse population with genuinely different assessments of what strategies for liberation were viable given the realities of American racism. A correctly identifies this diversity as analytical insight rather than weakness. B presents a false dichotomy and oversimplifies both positions. C misrepresents both strategies as equally rejecting mainstream engagement. D makes an unsupported empirical claim about the majority of African Americans' political preferences.
items.explanationEs: La coexistencia de estrategias integracionistas y nacionalistas dentro del pensamiento político negro refleja que los afroamericanos no eran una comunidad política monolítica sino una población diversa con evaluaciones genuinamente diferentes sobre qué estrategias de liberación eran viables dadas las realidades del racismo estadounidense. A identifica correctamente esta diversidad como perspicacia analítica más que debilidad. B presenta una falsa dicotomía y simplifica en exceso ambas posiciones. C malinterpreta ambas estrategias como rechazando igualmente el compromiso convencional. D hace una afirmación empírica sin apoyo sobre las preferencias políticas de la mayoría de los afroamericanos.

items.stem: Zora Neale Hurston conducted extensive fieldwork documenting African American folklore in the South, arguing in her academic work and novels that Black folk culture was a rich, sophisticated, living tradition — not a degraded remnant of slavery but an active creative system. Some contemporaries, including Richard Wright, criticized Hurston's work for failing to sufficiently address racial oppression and for potentially providing white audiences with a comforting, apolitical view of Black life. Evaluate these competing assessments of Hurston's work.
items.stemEs: Zora Neale Hurston realizó extenso trabajo de campo documentando el folclore afroamericano en el Sur, argumentando en su trabajo académico y novelas que la cultura folclórica negra era una tradición rica, sofisticada y viva, no un remanente degradado de la esclavitud sino un sistema creativo activo. Algunos contemporáneos, incluido Richard Wright, criticaron el trabajo de Hurston por no abordar suficientemente la opresión racial y por potencialmente proporcionar a las audiencias blancas una visión cómoda y apolítica de la vida negra. Evalúa estas evaluaciones en competencia del trabajo de Hurston.

choices.text: Hurston's critics were entirely correct: any artistic work that celebrates Black culture without explicitly addressing oppression is politically irresponsible.
choices.textEs: Los críticos de Hurston tenían completamente razón: cualquier obra artística que celebre la cultura negra sin abordar explícitamente la opresión es políticamente irresponsable.

choices.text: Hurston was entirely correct: celebrating Black folk culture's sophistication was always politically valuable regardless of how white audiences might receive or misappropriate it.
choices.textEs: Hurston tenía completamente razón: celebrar la sofisticación de la cultura folclórica negra siempre fue políticamente valioso independientemente de cómo las audiencias blancas pudieran recibirla o inapropiársela.

choices.text: Both assessments are partially valid: Hurston's cultural affirmation challenged degrading representations of Black life, while the concern about apolitical reception revealed a genuine tension in creating art for a racially hostile audience.
choices.textEs: Ambas evaluaciones son parcialmente válidas: la afirmación cultural de Hurston desafió representaciones degradantes de la vida negra, mientras que la preocupación por la recepción apolítica reveló una tensión genuina en crear arte para una audiencia racialmente hostil.

choices.text: The debate between Hurston and her critics was purely a personal rivalry with no substantive artistic or political content underlying their disagreements.
choices.textEs: El debate entre Hurston y sus críticos fue puramente una rivalidad personal sin ningún contenido artístico o político sustantivo subyacente a sus desacuerdos.

items.explanation: Both assessments capture something real: Hurston's celebration of Black folk culture was a genuine act of cultural affirmation that countered degrading representations, while Wright's concern about apolitical readings was also legitimate given the potential for white audiences to appreciate Black culture while ignoring Black suffering. The debate reflects a genuine tension in Black artistic production about how to represent community life when that representation will be consumed by a racially hostile society. C presents the most analytically sophisticated evaluation. A uncritically accepts one side. B uncritically dismisses one side. D misrepresents the debate as purely personal.
items.explanationEs: Ambas evaluaciones capturan algo real: la celebración de Hurston de la cultura folclórica negra fue un genuino acto de afirmación cultural que contrarrestó representaciones degradantes, mientras que la preocupación de Wright sobre las lecturas apolíticas también era legítima dado el potencial de que las audiencias blancas apreciaran la cultura negra mientras ignoraban el sufrimiento negro. El debate refleja una tensión genuina en la producción artística negra sobre cómo representar la vida comunitaria cuando esa representación será consumida por una sociedad racialmente hostil. C presenta la evaluación analíticamente más sofisticada. A acepta acriticamente un lado. B descarta acriticamente un lado. D malinterpreta el debate como puramente personal.

items.stem: The Jazz Age of the 1920s saw a cultural crossing of racial lines in music and entertainment — white musicians adopted and often commercialized jazz and blues forms originally developed by Black artists. Historians have debated whether this represented cultural exchange, appropriation, or something more complex. What framework most accurately captures the dynamics of this racial boundary crossing in 1920s popular culture?
items.stemEs: La Era del Jazz de la década de 1920 vio un cruce cultural de líneas raciales en la música y el entretenimiento: músicos blancos adoptaron y a menudo comercializaron formas de jazz y blues originalmente desarrolladas por artistas negros. Los historiadores han debatido si esto representó un intercambio cultural, apropiación, o algo más complejo. ¿Qué marco captura con mayor precisión la dinámica de este cruce de fronteras raciales en la cultura popular de la década de 1920?

choices.text: Genuine artistic exchange and structural racial inequality coexisted — real cross-cultural influence flowed in multiple directions, but Black artists faced structural barriers to commercial access and financial reward that white artists did not.
choices.textEs: El intercambio artístico genuino y la desigualdad racial estructural coexistían: la influencia intercultural real fluyó en múltiples direcciones, pero los artistas negros enfrentaban barreras estructurales para el acceso comercial y la recompensa financiera que los artistas blancos no enfrentaban.

choices.text: The racial crossing in 1920s popular culture represented pure cultural exchange with equal benefit to all parties, as Black and white artists freely chose to collaborate and share musical ideas.
choices.textEs: El cruce racial en la cultura popular de la década de 1920 representó un intercambio cultural puro con igual beneficio para todas las partes, ya que los artistas negros y blancos elegían libremente colaborar y compartir ideas musicales.

choices.text: All racial boundary crossing in 1920s music was straightforward appropriation, where white artists stole Black culture without any genuine artistic exchange or mutual influence.
choices.textEs: Todo cruce de fronteras raciales en la música de la década de 1920 fue una apropiación directa, donde los artistas blancos robaron la cultura negra sin ningún intercambio artístico genuino o influencia mutua.

choices.text: The question of whether cross-racial musical exchange was appropriation or exchange is entirely subjective and cannot be analyzed using historical frameworks.
choices.textEs: La pregunta de si el intercambio musical interracial fue apropiación o intercambio es completamente subjetiva y no puede analizarse usando marcos históricos.

items.explanation: The jazz/blues crossing involved both genuine cultural exchange (real artistic influence flowed in multiple directions) and structural inequality (white artists gained commercial access and financial reward that Black artists often could not access). The presence of both exchange and exploitation makes simplistic 'pure exchange' or 'pure appropriation' frameworks inadequate. A correctly identifies this complexity. B presents the 'pure exchange' framing that ignores structural inequality. C presents the 'pure appropriation' framing that ignores genuine artistic exchange and influence. D avoids the question rather than answering it with a framework.
items.explanationEs: El cruce del jazz/blues involucró tanto un intercambio cultural genuino (la influencia artística real fluyó en múltiples direcciones) como una desigualdad estructural (los artistas blancos ganaron acceso comercial y recompensa financiera a la que los artistas negros a menudo no podían acceder). La presencia de tanto intercambio como explotación hace inadecuados los marcos simplistas de 'intercambio puro' o 'apropiación pura'. A identifica correctamente esta complejidad. B presenta el encuadre de 'intercambio puro' que ignora la desigualdad estructural. C presenta el encuadre de 'apropiación pura' que ignora el intercambio artístico genuino y la influencia. D evita la pregunta en lugar de responderla con un marco.

items.stem: The New Negro movement of the 1920s, articulated by Alain Locke's 1925 anthology "The New Negro," argued that African Americans needed to shed the psychologically damaging effects of accommodation to white supremacy and develop a new cultural self-confidence rooted in African American artistic and intellectual achievement. How does this cultural-psychological argument complement or diverge from the political-legal strategies of the NAACP?
items.stemEs: El movimiento del Nuevo Negro de la década de 1920, articulado por la antología de Alain Locke de 1925 'The New Negro', argumentaba que los afroamericanos necesitaban desprenderse de los efectos psicológicamente dañinos de la acomodación a la supremacía blanca y desarrollar una nueva autoconfianza cultural arraigada en el logro artístico e intelectual afroamericano. ¿Cómo complementa o diverge este argumento cultural-psicológico de las estrategias político-legales de la NAACP?

choices.text: The New Negro movement directly opposed the NAACP's strategies, arguing that legal approaches were useless and only cultural transformation could achieve racial equality.
choices.textEs: El movimiento del Nuevo Negro se opuso directamente a las estrategias de la NAACP, argumentando que los enfoques legales eran inútiles y que solo la transformación cultural podía lograr la igualdad racial.

choices.text: The New Negro movement and the NAACP occupied entirely separate spheres — cultural and legal — with no overlap in goals, methods, or key figures.
choices.textEs: El movimiento del Nuevo Negro y la NAACP ocupaban esferas completamente separadas — cultural y legal — sin superposición en objetivos, métodos o figuras clave.

choices.text: The two approaches operated at complementary levels — legal strategy challenged structural racial hierarchy while cultural self-affirmation challenged the psychological internalization of inferiority that legal equality alone could not address.
choices.textEs: Los dos enfoques operaban en niveles complementarios: la estrategia legal desafiaba la jerarquía racial estructural mientras que la autoafirmación cultural desafiaba la internalización psicológica de la inferioridad que la igualdad legal por sí sola no podía abordar.

choices.text: Cultural transformation was always more powerful than legal reform as a strategy for racial equality, and the New Negro movement ultimately achieved more than the NAACP's legal campaigns.
choices.textEs: La transformación cultural siempre fue más poderosa que la reforma legal como estrategia de igualdad racial, y el movimiento del Nuevo Negro finalmente logró más que las campañas legales de la NAACP.

items.explanation: The New Negro cultural approach and NAACP legal strategy operated at different but complementary levels: the NAACP challenged the legal structures of racial hierarchy, while the New Negro movement challenged the psychological internalization of inferiority that legal equality alone could not address. Both were necessary for complete liberation, addressing structural and internal dimensions of oppression respectively. C captures this complementary multi-level analysis. A presents an oversimplified conflict between the approaches that misrepresents both. B is empirically inaccurate; the NAACP did engage in cultural work and Locke's movement engaged in political argument. D presents a false dichotomy between culture and politics as liberation strategies.
items.explanationEs: El enfoque cultural del Nuevo Negro y la estrategia legal de la NAACP operaban en niveles diferentes pero complementarios: la NAACP desafiaba las estructuras legales de la jerarquía racial, mientras que el movimiento del Nuevo Negro desafiaba la internalización psicológica de la inferioridad que la igualdad legal por sí sola no podía abordar. Ambos eran necesarios para la liberación completa, abordando respectivamente las dimensiones estructurales e internas de la opresión. C captura este análisis complementario multinivel. A presenta un conflicto simplificado en exceso entre los enfoques que malinterpreta ambos. B es empíricamente inexacto; la NAACP sí se involucró en trabajo cultural y el movimiento de Locke se involucró en argumentos políticos. D presenta una falsa dicotomía entre cultura y política como estrategias de liberación.

items.stem:
Read the following poem by Langston Hughes, "I, Too," first published in Library of Congress, Harlem Renaissance Collection (loc.gov), March 1925 (public domain):

"I, too, sing America.
I am the darker brother.
They send me to eat in the kitchen
When company comes,
But I laugh,
And eat well,
And grow strong.

Tomorrow,
I'll be at the table
When company comes.
Nobody'll dare
Say to me,
'Eat in the kitchen,'
Then.

Besides,
They'll see how beautiful I am
And be ashamed—
I, too, am America."

Using this poem and your knowledge of the Harlem Renaissance (US.32) and its relationship to the broader social conditions African Americans faced in the 1920s (US.37, US.29), write a 1–2 paragraph CER response that claims what the Harlem Renaissance represented as a form of political and cultural resistance. Support your claim with evidence from the poem and from your knowledge of specific Harlem Renaissance figures and events, and provide reasoning that explains why artistic expression became a vehicle for challenging racial inequality in this era.
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente poema de Langston Hughes, "Yo también", publicado por primera vez en Survey Graphic, marzo de 1925 (dominio público):

"Yo también canto a América.
Soy el hermano más oscuro.
Me mandan a comer en la cocina
cuando llegan las visitas,
pero yo me río,
y como bien,
y me hago fuerte.

Mañana
estaré en la mesa
cuando lleguen las visitas.
Nadie se atreverá
a decirme:
'Come en la cocina',
entonces.

Además,
verán lo hermoso que soy
y se avergonzarán—
Yo también soy América."

Usando este poema y tu conocimiento del Renacimiento de Harlem (US.32) y su relación con las condiciones sociales más amplias que enfrentaban los afroamericanos en la década de 1920 (US.37, US.29), escribe una respuesta CER de 1 a 2 párrafos que afirme qué representó el Renacimiento de Harlem como forma de resistencia política y cultural. Apoya tu afirmación con evidencia del poema y de tu conocimiento de figuras y eventos específicos del Renacimiento de Harlem, y proporciona razonamiento que explique por qué la expresión artística se convirtió en un vehículo para desafiar la desigualdad racial en esta era.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response will: (1) Claim—e.g., 'The Harlem Renaissance was not merely a cultural flowering but a deliberate assertion of Black humanity and citizenship rights in the face of systemic racial exclusion, deploying art and literature as forms of protest where political avenues remained blocked.' (2) Evidence from the poem: 'I, too, am America' as a direct claim to full citizenship; the kitchen as metaphor for segregation and forced invisibility; the future tense ('Tomorrow, I'll be at the table') as defiant optimism and long-term political aspiration. items.stem: The Harlem Renaissance of the 1920s produced literature, music, visual art, and social criticism that engaged explicitly with questions of racial identity, African American history, and the experience of living under white supremacy. How should historians evaluate the Harlem Renaissance as a political phenomenon in addition to its considerable cultural achievements?

choices.text: The Harlem Renaissance represented a form of cultural politics in which Black artists and intellectuals used creative expression to directly challenge racial inferiority narratives embedded in American culture — claiming full intellectual and creative authority in a society that legally and socially denied Black people equal standing.

The Harlem Renaissance was primarily a demographic phenomenon enabled by the Great Migration's concentration of Black talent in Northern cities, and its political dimensions were secondary to its cultural outputs since most participants rejected explicit political advocacy in favor of aesthetic achievement.

Because most Harlem Renaissance artists prioritized artistic quality over political messaging, the movement's political significance lies in what it later inspired rather than in any direct challenge to the racial order that its participants themselves undertook or articulated.

The Harlem Renaissance's political impact was substantially limited by its dependence on white patronage, its concentration in the Northern middle class, and its focus on New Negro ideals of uplift — meaning it failed to directly address the economic immiseration and racial violence confronting most Black Americans in the South and in Northern working-class communities.

items.explanation: The Harlem Renaissance was inherently political because the creation of a demonstrably rich and sophisticated Black American artistic culture directly contested the intellectual foundation of white supremacy — making cultural production itself a form of political contestation against the racial hierarchy.

items.stem: Which best describes the long-term significance of women's mass entry into industrial labor during World War II?

choices.text: Wartime industrial participation permanently eliminated gender-based wage discrimination in the American manufacturing sector.
Women's entry into industrial work demonstrated that wartime necessity could rapidly erode long-standing social barriers, even though many of those gains were reversed after the war ended.
Women entered industrial roles primarily in supervisory and management positions, transforming the organizational structure of American factories.
The federal government recruited women for factory work mainly to compensate for labor shortfalls created by the decline of agricultural employment.

items.explanation: Millions of women entered industrial labor during WWII, challenging gender-based employment norms. However, at war's end, many were displaced by returning veterans, and the pre-war pay and role disparities largely reasserted themselves — demonstrating both the possibility and the limits of wartime social change.

items.stemEs: ¿De qué maneras contribuyó el Renacimiento de Harlem a la lucha a largo plazo por los derechos civiles?

choices.text: It had no lasting impact because the movement ended during the Great Depression and was forgotten
It directly resulted in the passage of federal civil rights legislation during the 1920s
It built a foundation of cultural pride, intellectual achievement, and shared identity that empowered later generations of civil rights activists
It achieved full racial equality through artistic expression alone, making political activism unnecessary

items.explanation: The Harlem Renaissance fostered a powerful sense of cultural identity and pride among African Americans. Writers, artists, and musicians created works that challenged racial hierarchies and inspired future civil rights leaders. The movement's legacy provided an intellectual and cultural foundation for the activism of the 1950s and 1960s.

items.stem: African Americans in the 1920s faced persistent racial violence, political disenfranchisement, and economic marginalization — yet the same decade produced the Harlem Renaissance, the rise of Marcus Garvey's mass movement, and the Jazz Age. Using your knowledge of the Harlem Renaissance (US.32), Jazz Age cultural changes (US.33), and Marcus Garvey's Black nationalism (US.37), write an extended essay that argues how African Americans in the 1920s responded to racial oppression and what those responses reveal about the possibilities and limits of resistance in a segregated society. Your essay must: (1) state a clear, defensible claim; (2) provide specific evidence from all three standards; (3) compare at least two distinct strategies or forms of Black resistance; and (4) synthesize across the three standards to assess which approach held the greatest potential for long-term change and why. Your essay should be 4–6 well-developed paragraphs.
items.stemEs: Los afroamericanos en los años 1920 enfrentaron violencia racial persistente, privación del derecho al voto y marginación económica — sin embargo, la misma década produjo el Renacimiento de Harlem, el surgimiento del movimiento masivo de Marcus Garvey y la Era del Jazz. Usando tu conocimiento del Renacimiento de Harlem (US.32), los cambios culturales de la Era del Jazz (US.33) y el nacionalismo negro de Marcus Garvey (US.37), escribe un ensayo extendido que argumente cómo los afroamericanos en los años 1920 respondieron a la opresión racial y qué revelan esas respuestas sobre las posibilidades y los límites de la resistencia en una sociedad segregada. Tu ensayo debe: (1) formular una afirmación clara y defendible; (2) proporcionar evidencia específica de los tres estándares; (3) comparar al menos dos estrategias distintas o formas de resistencia negra; y (4) sintetizar a través de los tres estándares para evaluar qué enfoque tenía mayor potencial para el cambio a largo plazo y por qué. Tu ensayo debe tener 4–6 párrafos bien desarrollados.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response (4/4) will include: (1) A nuanced claim—e.g., 'While no single strategy succeeded in dismantling Jim Crow in the 1920s, the Harlem Renaissance's assertion of Black artistic and intellectual dignity laid the ideological groundwork for the Civil Rights Movement of the 1950s–60s, whereas Garvey's mass mobilization demonstrated the depth of Black political aspiration but ultimately failed due to state repression and organizational difficulties.' (2) Evidence across three standards: US.32—Hughes, Hurston, Cullen, McKay; Library of Congress, NAACP Records (loc.gov) magazine; NAACP; assertion of Black intellectual equality; 'double consciousness'; US.33—jazz and blues as cultural assertion moving northward via the Great Migration; Harlem jazz clubs as spaces of Black freedom; radio broadcasting jazz nationally; US.37—UNIA 2+ million members; Black Star Line; Pan-African ideology; FBI/Hoover surveillance; Garvey's deportation (1927). (3) Comparison: Harlem Renaissance worked within American cultural space, claiming Black Americans' place in American civilization; Garvey rejected that space entirely, seeking an independent Black nation. Jazz occupied a middle position—Black-created but crossing racial lines, eventually appropriated by white artists. (4) Synthesis: The coexistence of these strategies reveals that the structural barriers to Black equality were so total that no single approach commanded consensus; the 1920s created the intellectual and organizational infrastructure (NAACP, Black press, cultural confidence) that would later sustain the Civil Rights Movement (US.71–US.77).

items.stem: The 1920s produced competing visions of what the African American future in the United States should look like. Using your knowledge of the Harlem Renaissance (US.32), Marcus Garvey and Black nationalism (US.37), and the Jazz Age (US.33), write an extended essay that analyzes the following question: Did the cultural achievements of the Harlem Renaissance and the Jazz Age advance or undermine Marcus Garvey's vision of Black self-determination and economic independence? Your essay must: (1) articulate both the Harlem Renaissance/Jazz Age vision and the Garveyite vision of Black progress clearly enough to compare them; (2) use specific evidence from all three standards to analyze areas of agreement, tension, or contradiction between these visions; (3) evaluate the extent to which each approach addressed the lived realities of African Americans in the 1920s (including racism, segregation, and economic exclusion); and (4) synthesize across standards to reach a defensible conclusion about which approach offered a more viable path toward racial equality and why. Your essay should be 4–6 well-developed paragraphs.
items.stemEs: Los años 1920 produjeron visiones competitivas sobre cómo debería ser el futuro afroamericano en los Estados Unidos. Usando tu conocimiento del Renacimiento de Harlem (US.32), Marcus Garvey y el nacionalismo negro (US.37), y la Era del Jazz (US.33), escribe un ensayo extendido que analice la siguiente pregunta: ¿Los logros culturales del Renacimiento de Harlem y la Era del Jazz promovieron o socavaron la visión de Marcus Garvey de la autodeterminación y la independencia económica negra? Tu ensayo debe: (1) articular tanto la visión del Renacimiento de Harlem/Era del Jazz como la visión garveísta del progreso negro con suficiente claridad para compararlas; (2) usar evidencia específica de los tres estándares para analizar áreas de acuerdo, tensión o contradicción entre estas visiones; (3) evaluar en qué medida cada enfoque abordó las realidades vividas de los afroamericanos en los años 1920 (incluyendo el racismo, la segregación y la exclusión económica); y (4) sintetizar entre estándares para llegar a una conclusión defendible sobre qué enfoque ofrecía un camino más viable hacia la igualdad racial y por qué. Tu ensayo debe tener 4–6 párrafos bien desarrollados.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response (4/4) will include: (1) Clear articulation of both visions: Harlem Renaissance/Jazz Age — cultural integration, proving Black artistic and intellectual equality within American society; key figures: Langston Hughes, Zora Neale Hurston, Duke Ellington, Louis Armstrong; Garvey — Universal Negro Improvement Association (UNIA), 'Back to Africa,' Black Star Line, economic self-sufficiency, racial pride separate from white American society. (2) Comparative analysis across standards — areas of agreement: both rejected the idea of Black inferiority, both promoted racial pride; areas of tension: Garvey criticized Harlem Renaissance intellectuals as seeking validation from white society; Du Bois (linked to Harlem Renaissance) criticized Garvey's separatism and had him deported; jazz was commercialized by white-owned record labels and venues that excluded Black ownership. (3) Lived realities: Great Migration as context (Black Southerners fleeing Jim Crow to Northern cities); Tulsa Race Massacre (1921) — Garvey's economic nationalism arose directly from such destruction; redlining; job discrimination; neither cultural achievement nor separatist emigration fully addressed structural racism. (4) Synthesis: defensible conclusion — e.g., Harlem Renaissance created lasting cultural capital but operated within a white-controlled cultural economy; Garvey's economic nationalism was visionary but organizationally flawed; both responses were genuine but neither alone sufficient given the structural scale of American racism.
